run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T21:59:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert's error-rate deviation traces to a ~2-3 minute outage of the payment service at about 21:51-21:53, during and after the payment Deployment was rolled out at 21:49:30. Observed facts: frontend-proxy ingress error spans jumped by ~70 (514->584 between 21:50 and 21:53) while checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and its server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder each added exactly 69 error spans, frontend's POST /api/checkout added the same 69, and payment itself logged no errors and recorded no error status on its charge spans, receiving no charge requests from ~21:51 to ~21:53. The payment pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 was killed at 21:49:33 and replaced by payment-54499f9786-4r25d (container started 21:49:33, Ready, 0 restarts); the new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 differs from payment-55766d76b9 only by the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T21:49:30Z, with the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and identical env, and the payment container has no readiness/liveness/startup probe. The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds the only switched-on fault-injection setting: paymentUnreachable, defaultVariant "on", description "Payment service is unavailable"; every other fault flag in that file is off. Hypothesis: that setting is what made payment unreachable to checkout at 21:51-21:53 (the object holding the fault), with the 21:49:30 restart as its mechanism; an alternative, indistinguishable mechanism is a rollout readiness gap, since the single, probe-less payment pod was replaced at the same instant and only began receiving charge spans again at ~21:54. Conclusion is partial: the currently-on flag does not correspond to any ongoing Charge failure in the sampled data (charges succeed again from 21:54), who switched it on and when is unobservable (no change history, no flagd logs), and the declared fault itself was not directly observed.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ingress error-span counter rose from 514 at 21:50 to 543 at 21:51 and 583 at 21:52 and 584 at 21:53, i.e. ~70 new error spans in about two minutes, after which it crept by roughly one span per minute (585 at 21:56, 589 at 22:01, 593 at 22:05).

The same burst is visible one layer down: frontend span POST /api/checkout error counter was 87 from 21:28 through 21:50, 115 at 21:51 and 156 at 21:52 (+69, then flat), while checkout span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge error counter went 28 at 21:51 to 69 at 21:52 and stayed 69 through 22:10.

At 22:05 the cumulative error-span counters were: checkout 69 on oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and 69 on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; frontend 156 on POST /api/checkout, 156 on executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and 156 on grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; frontend-proxy 593 on ingress and 504 on router frontend egress. Payment's own error counters were only 4 on GET, 2 on dns.lookup and 2 on tcp.connect.

Across 25-minute windows by service and span, only checkout (oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, ~42 per 25 min), frontend (POST /api/checkout and related spans), and frontend-proxy (ingress, router frontend egress) carry the burst; ad and fraud-detection show only ~1-3 errors per 25 min on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, recommendation 1-3 on /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, and accounting and payment show 0.

Payment's own spans carry no error status: span_name charge and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge exist only with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (~805 spans per 25 min at 21:55), and the 2-minute increase of payment's charge spans fell to 8 at 21:51, 0 at 21:52 and 0 at 21:53, then recovered to 60 at 21:54 - i.e. no charge requests reached payment for about two to three minutes.

The payment pod was replaced during the window: events show Deployment payment scaling up ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1 at 21:49:30, Pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled 21:49:30 and container payment Started 21:49:33, Pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 Killing at 21:49:33, ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 Deleted pod at 21:49:33, and Deployment payment scaling down payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0 at 21:49:33.
The restarted payment pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d was created at 2026-11-17T21:49:30Z, is Running and Ready=True with restartCount 0, while all other otel-demo pods were created at 21:17.

The new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 (deployment revision 2, 1 replica) and the old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (revision 1, 0 replicas) both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE, PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES); the only template difference shown is pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T21:49:30Z on the new ReplicaSet.
Deployment payment has replicas=1, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%, and its payment container defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json defines flag paymentUnreachable with state ENABLED, defaultVariant "on", variants {off: false, on: true} and description "Payment service is unavailable" - the value in effect is on, not off/false.

Every other fault-injection flag in the same flagd-config demo.flagd.json is off: adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all have defaultVariant "off".

After the burst the payment dependency works again in the sampled data: payment container logs from 21:54:03 to 22:03:27 consist of paired "Charge request received." / "Transaction complete." lines with no error lines, checkout logs at 22:02:08-22:03:29 say "payment went through", and frontend-proxy access logs at 21:56:19-21:57:59 show POST /api/checkout answered 200 (with a few 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET /api/products and /api/cart).

An earlier, separate error episode predates the deviation: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data error counters were already 343 at 21:28 and remained exactly 343 through 22:10, and frontend-proxy's ingress error counter was already 505 at 21:28.

The payment Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment matches the payment Deployment's pod-template label opentelemetry.io/name=payment, and an Endpoints object otel-demo/payment exists; the payment probe-less container was therefore routable as soon as it started.

The only metric names matching traces_|http_|rpc_|app_ in the window are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so all error-rate evidence here comes from span-derived counters.

The paymentUnreachable flag is currently "on" yet Charge calls succeed in the same sampled window: checkout's Charge error counter froze at 69 from 21:52 to 22:10, payment logged only successful charges from 21:54 and checkout logged "payment went through" - so the flag's current on-state does not correspond to any observed ongoing payment outage, and it cannot be confirmed from these signals alone that it caused the 21:51-21:53 burst.

An image or code change on the payment Deployment caused the failures - rejected: payment-54499f9786 and payment-55766d76b9 use the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and identical env, and differ only by the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt pod-template annotation.

Payment returned application-level charge failures (e.g. a paymentFailure injection) - rejected: paymentFailure has defaultVariant "off", payment's own charge / grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no error status, payment logs show paired successful transactions, and payment received no charge requests at all during the burst window.

Ad service failures produced the frontend-proxy error-rate deviation being alerted on - rejected: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data error counters were already 343 at 21:28 and never increased afterwards, so they are background from before the deviation, not the ~70-span burst at 21:51-21:53.

The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config with paymentUnreachable switched on ("Payment service is unavailable") is the fault that made the payment service unreachable to checkout at 21:51-21:53: it is the only switched-on fault-injection setting, its name and description refer to the payment service that was restarted with an unchanged pod template and that checkout reports as erroring, and no object other than that setting was seen applying a fault to payment.

An alternative, indistinguishable mechanism is a rollout readiness gap: at 21:49:30-21:49:33 the single payment replica was replaced (restartedAt annotation only), the new container started as the old pod was killed, the Deployment has no readiness probe so the new pod was Ready immediately and routable, and payment received no charge spans until ~21:54 - a gap of about 2-3 minutes that by itself accounts for the 69 failed Charge calls without any flag change.

Review the flagd change/audit history for otel-demo/flagd-config and confirm whether paymentUnreachable was switched to "on" around 21:49-21:53; if the injected payment outage is not wanted, set paymentUnreachable back to "off".

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) to the payment container so a restarted single-replica pod is not added to the payment Service endpoints before it accepts connections; the current probe-less template makes every restart/rollout a potential payment outage.

Find who or what issued the payment rollout restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T21:49:30Z and whether it was part of the same change as the flagd flag update, since the restart timing and the flag are the two candidate triggers.

gaps: No change_history integration is available, so when and by whom paymentUnreachable was set to "on" and who issued the 21:49:30 rollout restart cannot be determined; the ConfigMap's creationTimestamp is 21:17:17 and its earlier data versions cannot be read.

The declared fault itself ("Payment service is unavailable") was not directly observed: no log line, event or trace shows the flag being evaluated or payment refusing/holding connections; the inference rests on checkout's error spans plus the absence of payment charge spans at 21:51-21:53.

Payment-side logs only reach back to 21:54:03 for the current container, the previous payment container instance is unavailable (old pod deleted), and the flagd/flagd-ui containers returned 0 bytes of logs, so behaviour between 21:49:33 and 21:54:03 and any flag-reload message are unknown.

Jaeger's newest available traces end at 21:45:00, before the burst, and traces_search/traces_search_by_tags for 21:50-22:15 returned no traces, so the failing Charge calls' error message and status detail could not be read.

No kube-state-metrics series were returned (get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing), so kube_pod_container_info/image_id, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_replicaset_owner and kube_pod_owner could not be checked; image identity and ready-replica history rest on current object state only.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the alert expression, its evaluation window and the reported value 0.0222 could not be reproduced or verified against the rule.
The frontend container produced no log lines in the queried window, so frontend-side error text for the failing /api/checkout requests is unavailable.

An earlier error episode (frontend AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data at 343 errors by 21:28, frontend-proxy ingress at 505 by 21:28) was not investigated to a cause; it ended before the deviation that matches the alert.
No NetworkPolicy objects were returned for namespace otel-demo, so network-policy interference cannot be positively excluded; the absence is the result of a query, not a cited finding.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and app_payment_transactions_total were not returned by get_metric_names in this window, so those request/latency/transaction signals are unknown rather than zero.
next_steps: Obtain the flagd change/audit log (or flagd-ui history) for otel-demo/flagd-config to establish when paymentUnreachable was switched to "on" and whether it overlapped 21:49-21:53.
Check the cluster's audit log / CI deployment history for the kubectl rollout restart applied to Deployment payment at 2026-11-17T21:49:30Z and for the paymentUnreachable edit.
If reproduction is possible, compare Charge call behaviour with paymentUnreachable on versus off and with a plain payment rollout to separate the flag effect from the readiness-gap effect.
After adding a payment readinessProbe, re-check whether a payment rollout still produces error spans on checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge.
